name: Sanctions & coercion
value: EU readies Iran sanctions; FMs meet 16 Nov
summary: EU working on new Iran sanctions after France blamed an IRGC unit for store cyberattacks; ministers meet 16 Nov
state: France attributed the October cyberattacks on refrigeration at hundreds of supermarkets to a unit linked to Iran's Revolutionary Guards on 10 Nov (Malay Mail). The same day an EU foreign affairs spokesman said the bloc is working on new sanctions against Iran, and foreign ministers are due to discuss them on 16 Nov (Diario Estrategia). No major economy has been cut off from payment systems and no large sovereign-asset seizure was found as of 13 Nov.
for_you: Firms trading with Iran, Russia or their intermediaries face a growing compliance burden as new listings are added; official guidance comes from OFSI, OFAC and the EU Council.
rubric_hit: Major new package in preparation (EU Iran measures; Watch); no payment-system cut-off or sovereign-asset seizure (Alert not met)

sources.title: Diario Estrategia — La UE trabaja en nuevas sanciones contra Irán tras ser señalado por los ciberataques a supermercados europeos
Malay Mail — France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guards for unprecedented supermarket fridge cyberattacks

why: Sanctions are now a frontline weapon; secondary sanctions and asset seizures fragment global finance and trade.
drivers: Russia/Iran sanctions packages, secondary sanctions, frozen-asset decisions, export controls.

rubric.alert: Major economy cut off from payment systems, or large-scale seizure of sovereign assets.

rubric.normal: No major new sanctions packages this week.
